newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends up on month-end export deals.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends up on month-end export deals.

text.p: Large month-end export deals pushed the Korean won to close higher against the dollar on Wednesday, traders said.

The local unit has regained some strength after hitting a six-year low of 834.50 on Tuesday, they said. It was the lowest level for the won since South Korea introduced a market average system in March 1990.
The won ended at an intraday high of 830.40 after opening at an intra-day low of 832.50.
"End-of-the-month export negotiations are putting a damper on the dollar," said one local dealer.

Traders said the won may strengthen to above the 830 level on Thursday on the back of further export demand. The won is expected to trade in a range of 829.50 to 831.50 on Thursday in cautious trading.
The base mid-rate for Thursday is forecast to be set at 831.30 against today's 833.60.
